A new open-access paper, **“A fragment-based model and annotation environment for discontinuous and overlapping terms”**, presents a framework for representing complex terminological structures as unified and directly inspectable annotation objects.

The work originated from a concrete annotation problem discussed during the preparation of the **ATE-IT 2026** challenge at EVALITA: how to represent terms that are discontinuous, overlap with one another, or share textual components. The resulting fragment-based model provides a common representation for contiguous, discontinuous, and overlapping terms.

The paper also introduces **Annotaterm**, a lightweight web-based environment supporting the annotation, visualization, editing, and export of these structures.

Developed in the context of the **HEREDITARY** project, this work has subsequently contributed to a broader modular framework for the annotation and curation of cultural heritage texts, to be presented at **IEEE-CH 2026**.
